findings.sourceReading: Kinzo says this is not a discussion that needs hiding, so Battler may stay. The scope is the imminent conversation.
findings.alternative: I have nothing to hide is often a conversational reassurance rather than a literal universal declaration. Nonetheless it enlarges a permission about this specific subject into a broad assertion about Kinzo secrets, losing the source limiting noun 話.

findings.sourceReading: Beato describes cruel and persistent people as usually prone to loneliness and lingering attachments. Neither comparative speed nor a temporal sequence is stated.
findings.alternative: Growing attached is related to lingering attachment, and the emotional connection survives. But quickest adds a comparative trait and then turns two concurrent tendencies into a sequence.

findings.sourceReading: Ange objects to Beato brazenly taking an unapologetic stance after the accusation: 開き直る. She is not asking why Beato has suddenly acquired a different character.
findings.alternative: A switch from accused to defiant can be described as a change in attitude. The following suspicion of trickery does not recover that objection.

Inherited118 amends held in gold-return context;131–132 recipient recovered direct address153;327–328 married couple recovered214;563 but omitted but hesitant/interrupted context preserves contrast;582 crime remains Ange’s accusation, not narrator-certified culprit fact.617 purpose/reason-to-live recovered616. findings.sourceReading: The children forget their original aim and begin shooting in order to survive; Ange similarly foresees hating in order to live. 生きるために makes survival the purpose served by the action.
findings.alternative: Living just to shoot or hate conveys fixation and can broadly describe the same ruined life. But it makes shooting or hatred the purpose of living rather than a means to continue living. The later English question shooting to live restores the source direction locally, limiting rather than removing this two-sentence reversal.
